title: The Power of God and the Nature of the Word
english: We have a discussion concerning God from the Scripture and from common understanding that He is unchangeable, and that He is immutable. For He who is not at all subject to quality does not turn, nor is He altered; for no alteration is anything other than a change according to quality. Not every change is an alteration, but the one according to quality. There are indeed also other changes, since there are also motions. That which becomes changes, but this motion is not an alteration. That which grows changes, but this is not an alteration; for such a motion is addition and increase. But when someone becomes lazy from being diligent, or lazy from being diligent, he is altered according to quality, just as when one comes from sickness to health and again.

But the words, regarding the meaning of the thing about which they are spoken, we understand. God was not composed of parts, since He is not composite; therefore, sitting upon Him, rising, walking, turning of the face, or illumination of the face, pass by. But in these things, regarding those arranged about Him, it is necessary to grasp the meaning in a God-befitting way to preserve faith. For some, through the words and their fluidity, subvert the things signified. Indeed, some have even dared to run into such a prosperity or impiety, so as to think the God human-shaped because of the manner in which they are written. And they say that God has hands, limbs, and feet, and appearance, and the rest. But if we know this always, regarding whom these things are said and from whom, we are able to lead the things to what is signified, to what is made manifest. If we do not grasp them in a God-befitting way, we are not able to have a pious conception concerning them according to each of the [words].

The prophets. For this one, in a certain place, says: 'Are not his words beautiful and rightly proceeding with him?' If they are not with him, according to his intention, they are not beautiful. If you hear—behold—sleep and wakefulness and repentance, and you do not receive such things according to his intention, then the things said about him do not rightly proceed with him.

But when you receive such things with him, the words proceeding rightly with him, being filled with spirit, have neither shadow nor sketch. This is what the Savior said in the Gospel: 'You wander, not knowing the Scriptures nor the power of God' (Matt 22:29). You wander, saying that he does not make things from non-being; for they say this: 'To do is later than to be; for there must exist something underlying. Those who are dead are without hope of resurrection.' Since, therefore, they do not receive these things through the power of God, because of this they stumble. God is able to bring from non-being into being and to transform corruptible bodies.

He says, then, to the Sadducees. He who thinks he knows the Scriptures wanders when he is ignorant of the power of God which is spoken concerning Him and by whom they are spoken. For whose sake these things have been spoken to me, I will say, apart from the deed about to take place. The Savior and our Lord is both God and man; God always, but not always man; for before the creation he was God, but not a man. And this also was destined to happen for the sake of salvation. And the becoming man has a cause, but being God is not because of a cause, but because of his own existence and the essence of his offspring; for thus I heard: 'I live because of the Father' (John 6:57) of mine.
